name: Mira220
description: ams OSRAM Mira220 - 1/2.7" 2.2 MP NIR-enhanced global shutter, mono 8/10/12-bit, MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY 2-lane up to 1.5 Gbit/s, max 90 fps @ full res. Verified against DS000642 v9-00 (2025-Sep) and Linux driver mira220.inl.
guide:
Mira220 quick guide (per DS000642 v9-00)
=========================================

- 1600x1400 active pixels (1642x1464 physical), 2.79 um pitch, BSI global shutter.
- 8/10/12-bit RAW, 90 fps @ 2.24 MP / 110 fps @ 1.4 MP / 255 fps @ VGA.
- MIPI CSI-2 v1.3 + D-PHY v1.2, 2 data + 1 clock lane, max 1.5 Gbit/s/lane.
- CCI: 16-bit register address, 8-bit data. I2C addr 0x54 (7-bit) -> 0xA8 (8-bit + W).
- Default cfg in this kit: 640x480 @ 80 fps, 12-bit RAW.

Key register groups
-------------------
  0x100C/100D  EXP_TIME       (LSB first!) exposure in row periods.
  0x1012/1013  VBLANK         framerate via Tframe = ROW_LEN*(VSIZE+VBLANK)/CLK.
  0x102B/102C  ROW_LENGTH     min 304 @ 1.5 Gbit/s 2-lane (8.2.2).
  0x107D..1081 VSTART (3 ROIs); 0x1087..108B VSIZE.
  0x2008/2009 HSIZE/2; 0x200A/200B HSTART/2; 0x207D/207E MIPI_HSIZE.
  0x1003       IMAGER_STATE   master = 0x10, slave = 0x08, force IDLE = 0x3F.
  0x10F0       IMAGER_RUN     self-clearing start-of-acquisition.
  0x209E       BIT_DEPTH      0x2=12b, 0x4=10b, 0x6=8b.
  0x209C/209D  HFLIP / HFLIP_B (per-context); 0x1095 VFLIP.
  0x2091       TEST_PATTERN_CFG bit[0]=enable, bits[6:4]=mode.
  0x205B/205C  RNC_DARK_TARGET 12-bit flat-field target (default 0x064).
  0x204B       RNC_EN         0x3 = enable row-noise correction.
  0x4006       BSP            0xF disable / 0x8 enable black-sun protection.
  0x6012       LANE           0 = 1 lane, 1 = 2 lanes.
  0x6013       CLK_MODE       0 = continuous, 1 = non-continuous.
  0x10D7/10D8  ILLUM_EN / ILLUM_POL (illumination strobe).

Notes
-----
- Temperature sensor is read at 0x3188/0x3189 (VPTAT) and 0x318E/0x318F (VREF);
  see datasheet 8.5.4 for the conversion formula.
- Frame counter is at 0x6016/0x6017 (MIPI FRAME_COUNTER), not 0x301x.
- OTP access uses 0x0080..0x008B (see 8.5.5), not 0x35xx.
- 0x4009 is a 6-bit X1 gain calibration value loaded from OTP 0x0A; not a 0..3 gain code.
- PLL multiplier/dividers are programmed via the common upload file (TRADE-SECRET
  registers, not in the public datasheet); only PLL_STATUS at 0x50DC is read-only.

tabs.controls: The cfg exposes Framerate and Exp(us) via the SDK. Analog gain is on the sensor (calibrated, not a simple 0..3). For experiments, write 0x4009 directly from the Sensor regs tab.
tabs.registers: Pick a register from the sensor profile dropdown to auto-fill the address. The 8 bit checkboxes stay in sync with the value field.
tabs.advanced: Increase USB transfer size for high-bandwidth modes (12b @ full res 90 fps). Apply between open() and start().

registers.name: Imager state
registers.help:
Per DS000642 Table 10. Writing this register stops or arms the acquisition FSM:

  0x02  Stop at the next row boundary (counters frozen, FSM -> IDLE)
  0x04  Stop at the next frame boundary (clean stop)
  0x08  Enter slave exposure control mode
  0x10  Enter master exposure control mode (what the SDK uses for streaming)
  0x3F  Force the imaging FSM to IDLE immediately

Reading 0x10 confirms the sensor is currently in master streaming mode. The reset/default value is 0x01.

registers.name: Imager run (start)
registers.help:
Write 1 to start a master-mode acquisition. Bit auto-clears.
Use IMAGER_STATE = 0x04 / 0x3F to stop.

registers.name: Run continuous
registers.help:
Bit 2 enables continuous run (writes 0x04). When clear, the sensor captures NB_OF_FRAMES (0x10F2/F3) and returns to IDLE.

Set to 0x04 to free-run.

registers.name: Power mode
registers.help:
DS000642 7.7. Default 0x0C = active.
  bit0 sleep enable, bit1 idle enable, bit2 system clk, bit3 SRAM clk.
See Figure 12 for the active/idle/sleep transitions.

registers.name: Soft reset
registers.help: Writes a soft reset pulse. Self-clearing. Useful to recover after MIPI errors without re-initialising the register bank.

registers.name: Exposure (rows)
registers.desc: EXP_TIME (16-bit) - integration time expressed in rows
registers.help:
Combined view of EXP_TIME (DS000642 §8.2.2). The hardware
expects the LSB written before the MSB; this entry performs both
writes in the correct order automatically.

T_exposure[s] = EXP_TIME * ROW_LENGTH / CLK_IN.

The SDK 'Exp(us)' control wraps the same two bytes; prefer that
control for live tuning, this entry is meant for raw debug.

registers.name: Exposure (rows) LSB
registers.desc: EXP_TIME [7:0] - LSB of exposure-time row count
registers.help: Write LSB before MSB (DS000642 ch.9). Total exposure = EXP_TIME * ROW_LENGTH * T_CLK_IN. The SDK 'Exp(us)' control wraps both bytes for you.

registers.name: VBLANK
registers.help:
Sets the framerate together with VSIZE and ROW_LENGTH:
  T_frame[s] = ROW_LENGTH * (VSIZE + VBLANK) / CLK_IN.

DS000642 Table 16 lists the recommended VBLANK values per ROI
and framerate. Increasing VBLANK lowers the framerate without
touching the exposure window.

registers.name: VBLANK LSB
registers.help: Drives the framerate. T_frame = ROW_LENGTH*(VSIZE+VBLANK)/CLK_IN. See Table 16 for the predefined VBLANK values per ROI/fps.

registers.name: ROW_LENGTH
registers.desc: ROW_LENGTH (16-bit) - line period in CLK_IN cycles
registers.help:
Sets the line rate. Minimum 304 with two D-PHY lanes at
1.5 Gbit/s; double it for single-lane and increase further for
slower MIPI rates (DS000642 Table 26).

Line rate[Hz] = CLK_IN / ROW_LENGTH.

registers.name: ROW_LENGTH LSB
registers.help: Sets the line rate. Minimum 304 with two D-PHY lanes at 1.5 Gbit/s. Double it for single-lane and increase further for slower MIPI rates (see DS000642 Table 26).

registers.name: NB_OF_FRAMES
registers.desc: NB_OF_FRAMES (16-bit) - frame count for non-continuous master mode
registers.help:
How many frames are produced before the FSM returns to IDLE
when RUN_CONT (0x1002) is cleared. Ignored in pipelined readout.

registers.name: Frames to capture LSB
registers.help: Number of frames before the sensor returns to IDLE in master non-continuous mode. Ignored in pipelined readout.

registers.name: Trigger source / pulse-width
registers.help:
Per Tab. 12 / 15:
  bit0 EXT_EXP_PW_SEL: 0 = exposure controlled by REQ_EXP pulse width, 1 = controlled by EXP_TIME register.
  bit6 EXT_EVENT_SEL: 0 = REQ_EXP starts readout (single-pin), 1 = REQ_FRAME starts readout (two-pin).
Default 0xD0.

registers.name: REQ_EXP (software)
registers.desc: CMD_REQ_EXP [0] - software equivalent of REQ_EXP pin

registers.name: REQ_FRAME (software)
registers.desc: CMD_REQ_FRAME [0] - software equivalent of REQ_FRAME pin (self-clearing)

registers.name: REQ_EXP delay
registers.desc: EXT_EXP_DELAY (16-bit) - rows between REQ_EXP and exposure
registers.help:
Programmable delay between REQ_EXP being asserted and the
actual start of integration. Useful to align the exposure window
with an external strobe.

Delay[s] = EXT_EXP_DELAY * ROW_LENGTH / CLK_IN.

registers.name: REQ_EXP delay LSB
registers.desc: EXT_EXP_DELAY [7:0] - delay (rows) between REQ_EXP and exposure

registers.name: VSTART1
registers.help:
First row of the readout window. Spans 0x107D[7:0] and
0x107E[2:0]. The upper bits of 0x107E (bits[7:3]) carry
VSTART2[4:0] for dual-ROI mode and are preserved by the GUI's
read-modify-write logic.

For a centred ROI of height H on the 1200-row array:
  VSTART1 = (1200 - H) / 2
  VSIZE1  = H

registers.name: VSIZE1
registers.help:
Vertical size of ROI #1. Spans 0x1087[7:0] and 0x1088[2:0].
The upper bits of 0x1088 (bits[7:3]) carry VSIZE2[4:0] for
dual-ROI mode and are preserved by the read-modify-write path.

Frame period: T_frame = ROW_LENGTH * (VSIZE1 + VBLANK) / CLK_IN.

registers.name: HSIZE
registers.desc: HSIZE (10-bit) - column count expressed as columns/2
registers.help:
Horizontal size of the readout window in pixel-pair units
(the array is read out in column pairs, see DS000642 §8.2.3).
For a width W in pixels: HSIZE = W / 2. Default 800 = full 1600.

registers.name: HSIZE LSB
registers.help: Width / 2 (datasheet 8.2.3 - the window is mirrored around the array centre line). Default 800 = 0x320 (full 1600).

registers.name: HSTART
registers.desc: HSTART (10-bit) - first column expressed as column/2
registers.help:
First column of the readout window in pixel-pair units.
For a centred ROI of width W: HSTART = (1600 - W) / 4.

registers.name: MIPI_HSIZE
registers.desc: MIPI_HSIZE (16-bit) - columns transmitted on CSI-2 (= 2 * HSIZE)
registers.help:
Total number of pixels per CSI-2 line. Must equal 2 * HSIZE
in normal operation. Mismatched values cause the host to drop
frames with a long-line / short-line error.

registers.name: VFLIP
registers.desc: VFLIP [0] - vertical flip (within ROI; ROI order unchanged)

registers.name: Bit depth
registers.help: Reduce bit depth to free MIPI bandwidth and reach higher fps. Remember to update CSI2_DTYPE (0x208D) accordingly: 0x4=12b, 0x2=10b, 0x1=8b.

registers.name: CSI-2 data type
registers.help: MIPI Data Type encoding. Must match BIT_DEPTH (0x209E).

registers.name: Histogram enable
registers.help: Computes a 32-bin histogram (+ clipped-black/white counters) for every frame. Sent as a CSI-2 Embedded-Data packet (0x12) at end-of-frame. See 8.5.3.

registers.name: Histogram usage ratio
registers.desc: HIST_USAGE_RATIO - spatial sub-sampling for the histogram

registers.name: Test pattern
registers.help:
DS000642 8.5.6:
  bit[0]   image-test-pattern enable
  bits[6:4] mode: 0=vertical gradient, 1=diagonal gradient,
                  4=walking 1's, 5=walking 0's

The combined values to write are therefore 0x00, 0x01, 0x11, 0x41, 0x51.
The Linux driver mira220.inl only exposes the first two values (Disable / Vertical gradient). Walking-1/0 patterns are useful to validate MIPI lane integrity.

Note: a 12-bit gradient fills the entire 0..4095 range, so without converting to 8-bit (>>4) it looks almost black on a uint16->uint8 display.

registers.name: Statistics control
registers.help:
bit1 PIXEL_DATA_SUPP: 0=send pixels and stats, 1=stats only.
bit2: enable statistic transmission.
Default 0x04 (stats off, pixels on).

registers.name: Black-sun protection
registers.help: Avoids dark-spot artefacts when extreme highlights saturate the pixel. The cfg in this kit writes 0x08 (enabled) at boot.

registers.name: DCDS - row-noise CDS
registers.desc: CDS_RNC [0] - column CDS in the row-noise pipeline

registers.name: DCDS - image
registers.desc: CDS_IMG [0] - column CDS on the image path

registers.name: Row-noise correction
registers.help: Enables on-chip row-noise correction (DCDS + per-row reference subtraction). The cfg writes 0x03 (enabled). See 6.4.2 / 8.4.4.

registers.name: Flat-field target LSB
registers.help: Target value (12-bit) for row-noise correction. Default 0x064 (=100). Refer to AN001032 before changing.

registers.name: Defect correction config
registers.desc: DC_CFG - bit0 enable, bit1 mode (0=2D,1=1D), bits[5:4] replacement
registers.help: Replacement value 0=median, 1=mean, 2=min, 3=max. Default 0x01 (enabled, 2D, median).

registers.name: X1 gain calibration
registers.help:
6-bit calibration value loaded from OTP address 0x0A on power-up (DS000642 8.5.5).

This is NOT a 0..3 gain code: do not use it as `0=1x, 1=2x ...`. Mira220 does not expose a public 0..3 analog-gain enum; gain steps are obtained through different ramp/PGA settings together with the PHY upload. Treat this register as a calibration trim only.

registers.name: Illumination enable
registers.desc: ILLUM_EN [0] - external strobe synchronous to exposure

registers.name: Lane count
registers.help: Single-lane mode requires doubling ROW_LENGTH (8.2.2).

registers.name: Clock mode
registers.help: Per DS000642: 0 = continuous, 1 = non-continuous. Most receivers prefer continuous.

registers.name: Frame mode
registers.desc: FRAME_MODE - 0 general / 1 accurate (image), bit1 same for embedded

registers.name: MIPI soft reset
registers.help: bit0 D-PHY, bit1 pixel clk, bit2 lane clk, bit3 byte clk, bit4 escape clk, bit5 APB clk.

registers.name: PLL status
registers.desc: PLL_STATUS - bit0 lock, bit1 ref-clock missing

registers.name: Frame counter (16-bit)
registers.desc: FRAME_COUNTER - 16-bit free-running, MSB at 0x6016, LSB at 0x6017
registers.help: Concatenates the two FRAME_COUNTER bytes (DS000642 §8.3.3, register 0x6016/0x6017) and shows the resulting 16-bit count both in decimal and hex. The counter periodically resets to 1 once it reaches the value programmed in 0x6016/17 (0x3C00 by default).

registers.name: Die temperature
registers.help:
Reads VPTAT (TSENS_SIG, 12 bits at 0x3188/0x3189) and VREF
(TSENS_RST, 10 bits at 0x318E/0x318F) and applies the
uncalibrated conversion from datasheet section 8.5.4.1:

  T[°C] = ((TSENS_SIG - TSENS_RST) * 0.181 - 140) / 1.63 + 25

A single-point calibration constant is stored in OTP (chuck
temperature, sig/rst at 60 °C). For higher accuracy, multiply
this raw temperature by Tchuck / Tcal (see DS000642 8.5.4.2).

Notes
-----
* The high bytes are masked (sig: bits[3:0], rst: bits[1:0]) to
  drop the reserved upper bits documented in the register map.
* The displayed `sig` / `rst` fields are the composed VPTAT and
  VREF values; `raw` is their difference (proportional to T).

registers.name: Temperature VPTAT (12-bit)
registers.desc: TSENS_SIG combined - voltage proportional to temperature

registers.name: Temperature VPTAT LSB
registers.desc: TSENS_SIG [7:0] - signal voltage proportional to temperature

registers.name: Drive strength
registers.desc: DRIVE_STRENGTH [2:0] - 2/4/8/12 mA digital, CCI sink select
registers.help:
bits[1:0]: digital outputs 0=2mA, 1=4mA, 2=8mA, 3=12mA.
bit[2]: CCI sink current 0=4mA, 1=20mA.
